title: Your Life as a Brine-Factor: The Ledger
protagonist: A debt-born Factor of the Skiff-Reaches, booked into an inherited balance before they could close their fist, who raised a foundling into the cant and then cleared their book by indenturing them — and still died in the red.

scenes.narration: The book is closing. The Toll runs near dry, your column is in front of the House, and your account will now be read aloud, cold and entire. You will not answer. You answered all your life. This is the House, and this is the reading of you.
scenes.image_prompt: Intimate close on a flat slab of dark salt-glass laid on a lashed plank beneath a low tarnished brass lamp, its face threaded with crystallized amber-and-teal veins of debt and credit incised as indecipherable scratched glyphs. A clerk's brass-scaled hand hovers poised above the stone, fingertips just touching the wet margin. Shallow brine glistens at the plank's edge, the lamp the only warmth in crowding shadow. Centered focal stone, hushed mercantile dread, subject kept clear of top and bottom edges.

scenes.narration: First line: you were booked before you could close your fist. A blank stone of dark salt-glass pressed into a palm too small to grip it, a brine-cord knotted at the wrist, a balance you never ran up entered against your name. You did not borrow. You were the collateral. Welcome to the Exchange, counterparty. You opened in the red.
scenes.image_prompt: Extreme close on a blank black salt-glass stone laid into an infant's open palm on cracked white crust, the small fingers half-curled and failing to close around it. A knotted brine-cord already binds the tiny wrist. Behind the hand the swollen rust-red sun lies doubled in a shrinking mirror-pool. Tender and cold at once, the unmarked stone the dark focal heart, low raking light, the hand and stone centered well clear of the frame edges.

scenes.narration: You worked the margins the other three orders left to crack. What the Mnemarchs would not sanctify, what the Iconoclasts had not yet smashed, what the Sediment had not dissolved — that off-cut glass was yours. Scavenger of scavengers, a debt with legs. You learned early the flat is no temple. It is a counting-table, and you were already on it.
scenes.image_prompt: Wide low-horizon establishing shot of a vast cracked salt-flat at low tide, bone-white hexagonal tiles ghosted with faint chalked parcel-marks like an auction grid of indecipherable scratches. A small barefoot debt-born child drags a salvage net of dull cracked off-cut glass across the crust, long shadow trailing. Distant ramshackle lashed skiffs hang hazed on the heat-shimmer, the doubled rust sun low. Crushing mercantile scale, lonely, leading lines of cracked tiles, the child kept off the bottom edge.

scenes.narration: Then you were taught the cant, because tender words cost more to feel. A friend is a counterparty. A death is a write-off. A clean book is a quiet little betrayal nobody contests. Every soft word has a ledger-word that prices cheaper, and you bought the whole vocabulary. You learned to laugh. The House notes you laughed early.
scenes.image_prompt: Intimate close on a young Factor grinning sidelong over a chalked slate scrawled with indecipherable incised marks, a brass-rimmed flask tilted in one hand, eyes bright and unreadable. Lamplight catches a low haze of iodine amber on the air and a careless scatter of pale faceted coin-cut salt tokens near the elbow. Charming, sly, faintly predatory warmth, tarnished key-light, deep shadow behind, the face and slate centered clear of the top and bottom edges.

scenes.narration: Now the credits. Your first lesson sat under all of them, the founding secret, quoted at par: a memory is worth not what happened, but what someone will pay to have happened. Truth is a commodity with a spread. You stopped grieving the gap between the two the day you learned to price it.
scenes.image_prompt: Transactional symmetry across a lashed counting-plank: one hand offers up a glowing half-spoiled salt-glass crystal, the other proffers a fistful of pale faceted salt tokens. The crystal is lit from within with a vague, smeared amber image, its detail dissolving into formless haze. Two tarnished brass lamps frame the exchange like scales coming to balance. Cold ritual stillness, the lit crystal and tokens the twin focal points, mirrored composition, hands kept clear of the frame edges.

scenes.narration: The order's whole position rests on one afternoon, taken here out of order because it is your true opening balance. Cassine Lir re-lived a battle that never was, edited the salt until it read as a Mnemarch triumph, and sold the lie back to the grieving for a skiff's weight of clean brine. No victory occurred. The First Ledger opened that afternoon, and you are a line in it.
scenes.image_prompt: Mid shot of a wading hauler kneeling over a crystal half-liquid in its shrinking pool, fingers trailing through the brine, coaxing it. Inside the glass a trapped image shifts from one dim massed indistinct shape into a brighter, triumphant arrangement of figures, still wordless and blurred. Iodine fog hangs close, the doubled rust sun low on the water behind. Quiet sacrilege, intent labor, the editing crystal the amber focal glow, the figure kept off the bottom edge.

scenes.narration: Your own first edited sale: a death smoothed, a price held, a buyer who thanked you for it. One coin-cut token, your first Coin, cold and faceted in the fist. You felt solvent. Mark that word. Solvency is the only joy the House stocks, and it sold you the whole feeling at retail. You came back for more.
scenes.image_prompt: Action diagonal: a young Factor skids a shallow brass-and-teal skiff away from a buyer's barge, laughing open-mouthed, one fist thrust up with a single pale coin-cut token catching the low light. Behind, the sold crystal already shrinks into a stranger's strongbox across the wet flat. Spray fans off the hull, the doubled rust sun rakes long shadows. Elated, kinetic, the raised token the bright focal point, motion sweeping off-frame, the figure kept clear of the top and bottom edges.

scenes.narration: Here is the arithmetic of a debt-born stone. The House prices your balance so the column never quite clears — not an error, the product, working exactly as designed. Pay all your life and you die one Coin short. There is one door out of the red, and only one. You put the whole balance onto another stone. You filed the thought away. It accrued.
scenes.image_prompt: Intimate close on a dark salt-glass ledger-stone held up against the rust-red sun, a single faint bright chalked credit dwarfed by a long crystallized column of deep-red debits glinting through the glass as indecipherable scratched glyphs. The holder's fingers grip tight and pale at the stone's edges. The doubled sun bleeds amber through the translucent slab. Cold revelation, the lit column the focal depth, the stone and fingers centered clear of the frame edges.

scenes.narration: Comradeship, too, was priced as a loan. Your Factor-Captain fronted your warband against your future custody, so you were in debt to your own commander before the first crystal was cut. Every truth you liquidated was a payment against yourself. You called him brother. The House files brother under interest-bearing.
scenes.image_prompt: Ritual-transactional symmetry on a ledger-barge: a weathered Factor-Captain presses a brine-flask of credited stock against a recruit's dark stone, the loan glowing amber as it seeps and crystallizes into the salt-glass. Behind them a roped flotilla of lashed skiffs rides the dark margin, lit by swaying tarnished brass lamps. The gesture is generous and binding at once. Cold intimacy, the glowing transfer the focal note, balanced framing, both figures kept clear of the top and bottom edges.

scenes.narration: On the very margin where you were found, you found one. A foundling, ribs like a net-frame, skimming cracked off-cut glass exactly as you once did. You watched from the skiff and your whole posture changed — the House marks the timestamp. Against every clause, against your own better book, you did not look away. You should have looked away. That line is held over.
scenes.image_prompt: Wide composition seen from a skiff's vantage: a small ragged foundling crouches on bared crust skimming dull off-cut glass into a frayed net, intent and unaware. From the dark water an older Factor watches, posture suddenly still with recognition, one hand frozen on the gunwale. The receding tide-line gleams behind, the doubled rust sun low, iodine haze softening the distance. Quiet ache, the watcher and child the twin focal poles, both kept off the bottom edge.

scenes.narration: You raised them into the cant, the runs, the laugh. You taught the small fingers which glass cracks clean and which is salvage. You shared brine that was not a loan. It was the one bond a Factor ever holds that is not a transaction, and the House does not file it under warmth. The House files it under your most dangerous, most valuable asset. The House will return to it.
scenes.image_prompt: Intimate close at dusk-eternal: two figures, one grown and one small, grinning together over a faintly glowing edited crystal balanced between their hands, lamplight warm on both faces. The moment is framed tenderly yet boxed in tight, like a thing about to be appraised and shelved. A soft iodine-amber glow gathers at the edges, deep shadow beyond. Rare unguarded warmth shadowed by foreboding, the shared crystal the focal heart, faces centered clear of the frame edges.

scenes.narration: The House pauses here. This bond is a line the reading will not yet take. Mark it sealed: account held over, carried forward, an open and unhedged position the House declines to price aloud at present. You think it forgotten. The House forgets nothing it can charge for. The seal stays on. It is keeping.
scenes.image_prompt: Ritual close on a dark ledger-stone set face-down on a plank and bound shut with a knotted brine-cord and a smear of wax-pale salt. A clerk's brass-scaled hand presses it sealed from above. One warm lamp throws a single edge of light; deep shadow crowds the rest. On the cord's small tag a lone indecipherable mark is scratched. Withheld, ominous stillness, the sealed stone the dark focal object, hand and stone kept clear of the top and bottom edges.

scenes.narration: Now the good years, totted out of order, because money keeps no calendar. You insured both sides of a war and collected on the breach — the only order to turn a profit on the death of a peace. While two faiths bled into the same pool, you stood between them chalking the price of each other's grief. The credits ran high. You laughed. It is here in your hand.
scenes.image_prompt: Wide action diagonal: a Factor stands on a tide-sledge in the middle distance, calmly chalking indecipherable marks on a slate between two distant clashing warbands — charcoal-ember figures to one side, oxidized verdigris figures to the other. Stacked pale coin-tokens sit at the Factor's feet. Smoke and bursting glass-dust rise on both far horizons, the doubled rust sun low between them. Cold profiteering amid carnage, the central Factor the still focal pivot, kept off the bottom edge.

scenes.narration: You could not hold still. To be stationary is to be unleveraged, and an unleveraged Factor is about to be liquidated by somebody faster. So you ran. You reached the glass, priced it mid-stride, took it, and were already gone before the ground knew you had stood on it. Keep it moving or it stops paying. You kept it moving for forty years.
scenes.image_prompt: Action diagonal of a barefoot Skiff-Reach runner skimming a shallow brass-and-teal skiff across just-dried crust, snatching a glowing amber crystal off the flat mid-stride without stopping. Spray fans wide, the abandoned ground already streaking away behind. Low raking rust light stretches the runner's shadow long across the cracked tiles. Pure restless momentum, the snatched crystal the bright focal note, sweeping motion to the frame edge, the runner kept clear of the top and bottom edges.

scenes.narration: Once you held a single breath too long on open ground. You felt it then in the body, the specific animal terror of the still — that you were a thing aimed at, a stationary asset about to be written down. You never froze again. The House respects this. Fear, properly leveraged, is just an early-warning system you never had to pay for.
scenes.image_prompt: Intimate close on a runner's face caught frozen mid-stride on bare open crust, eyes wide with a specific animal panic of standing still, oilskin slick with brine. A guarded glowing crystal glints just out of reach at the frame's edge. The vast empty drying flat seems to close in around the small still figure, the doubled rust sun low and pitiless. Held-breath dread, the panicked face the focal heart, framed clear of the top and bottom edges.

scenes.narration: You cut your brine with iodine on purpose, to blur which drowned afternoons were ever yours. The House taught you the principle and you drank to it: a clear conscience is only unrealized inventory, value sitting idle, refusing to move. So you blurred it, sold it forward, and felt nothing clean enough to slow you. Efficient. The House approves the entry.
scenes.image_prompt: Intimate close of a salt-glass flask raised to milky, unfocusing eyes, iodine-amber brine catching the lamplight as it tilts. The drinker's gaze drifts soft and far as memories smear and slide. A sweet medicinal amber haze hangs close around the face; shadow swallows everything beyond. Numb, deliberate self-erasure, the lit flask and clouding eyes the focal pair, warm key-light against deep gloom, the face kept clear of the top and bottom edges.

scenes.narration: You priced the three rivals and found them all arsonists at the warehouse. Set locks the stock in a vault no coin can open. Shatter burns it to glass-dust. Free dumps it into the pool for nothing at all. Three ways of taking inventory off the market and torching its value. Your only nightmare was simpler: the wrong past surviving while you held no position in it.
scenes.image_prompt: Wide symbolic triptych across one drying flat: at left a sealed glowing vault-crystal rimed in verdigris bronze, at center a crystal bursting into a cloud of glass-dust, at right a crystal dissolving freely into a teal pool. In the foreground a lone Factor turns away from all three, unimpressed, a chalk-stub in one hand. The doubled rust sun low behind. Cold mercantile contempt, three jewel focal accents across the basin, the Factor kept off the bottom edge.

scenes.narration: Now the debits, and the clock that calls them. The Toll runs toward dry; the brine pulls back fastest at the end, and your column has not cleared. The House does not threaten. The House simply lets you watch the water go and quotes you, in the quiet, the single price that clears your book. You already knew the number. You had known it since you were small.
scenes.image_prompt: Wide dread composition: a tarnished verdigris bell and a brine-glass hourglass running with iodine-tinted salt instead of sand stand on a barge at a fast-receding tide-line. Rows of bright exposed crystals line the bared crust like a filling sale-rack. The doubled rust sun sits low and swollen over the draining basin. Looming finality, the hourglass and bell the focal weights, the receding water a leading line, the objects kept clear of the top and bottom edges.

scenes.narration: Vael Surr, the Iodine Comptroller, did not give you an order. She does not deal in orders. She quoted you a price, and let you understand that a Factor who refuses her price finds no one will extend them brine on credit ever again. The price was the one asset large enough to settle the whole column. You did not ask what it was. You knew. Her own forearm carried the same old tally.
scenes.image_prompt: Intimate close on the Iodine Comptroller, eyes clouded iodine-amber, not pointing or commanding but tracing a single indecipherable mark in the air with one finger. The drying flat behind her seems to ripple and reprice at the gesture. A faint tally of incised scratched glyphs ghosts along her own bare forearm in the lamp-glow. Quiet, absolute authority, the clouded face and marking hand the focal pair, framed clear of the top and bottom edges.

scenes.narration: So the seal comes off. You laid your stone edge to edge with the apprentice's and let your whole balance bleed across — the red running out of you and clean into them, exactly as it was done to you before you could close your fist. You cut the cord. You ran. The cant has a word that lets you call it clearing your book. You used the word. It is the cleanest lie you ever sold.
scenes.image_prompt: Ritual close of two dark ledger-stones touched edge to edge on a plank, a whole crystallized balance bleeding from the larger going clean into the smaller, which floods red through the glass. A severed brine-cord and broken wax-pale salt lie beside them. One hand withdraws fast at the frame's edge; the other rests unaware in shadow. Betrayal as bookkeeping, the bleeding seam between the stones the focal heart, the stones centered clear of the edges.

scenes.narration: Here is the truth under every truth you traded. The Exchange is not a market of free men. It is a chain of inherited debt, each link pressed onto a smaller fist than the last. Clearing your book only forged the next link. You did not beat the House. You served it, faithfully, to the final entry. The one free trade — eat the loss, break the chain — is the single trade a Factor can never make. You came close enough to see it. Then you ran.
scenes.image_prompt: Vast symbolic wide: a long chain of identical knotted wrist-cords runs off across the bone-dry basin to the horizon, each link binding a smaller dark ledger-stone to a larger one, dwindling to nothing in the haze. The doubled rust sun sits behind. One near link has just snapped onto a small stone, the cord drawn taut as the tide pulls away. Crushing inevitability, the receding chain a leading line to the sun, the near link the focal point, kept off the bottom edge.

scenes.narration: You cashed out a heartbeat before the last pool dried, exactly as planned, with a clause drawn against every contingency but one. You never hedged sentiment. You looked back at a small fist on the margin — one glance, one breath of stillness — and that single uncovered exposure came due all at once. You ran the last yards short, and the Toll does not extend terms. You came up short.
scenes.image_prompt: Action diagonal of a lone Factor running a tide-sledge hard across nearly-dry crust toward the last guttering thread of brine, head turned a fraction backward in a glance that costs everything. Pale coin-tokens spill from a loosening fist. The tarnished verdigris Toll-bell hangs small behind, the doubled rust sun guttering low over a basin almost wholly drained. Fatal hesitation in motion, the spilling tokens the focal note, the figure kept clear of the top and bottom edges.

scenes.narration: You died owing more than you were owed. The only true disgrace, and you walked straight into it laughing. No pool fused you to itself. No blindness handed you the god undiluted. There was no revelation waiting, no kind last thing. There was only a column that would not clear, and a laugh still on the mouth when the mouth stopped. The House records the time.
scenes.image_prompt: Intimate close of a fallen Factor laid out on cracked white tiles, a faint grin frozen on the slack face, a single pale coin-token slipped from the open hand onto the salt. Cold flat light, no warm crystal anywhere near. The doubled rust sun lies dull in a thin nearby film of brine. Bleak, unredeemed stillness, the grinning face and dropped token the focal pair, the body laid low and kept clear of the bottom edge.

scenes.narration: They appraised you before they mourned you, because that is the order of operations and there was never any other. Brass-scaled hands turned your stone to the lamp and totted the crystallized column while you lay un-wept on the white tiles. The audit reached its bottom line. The bottom line read short. There was no second pass. There is no one left who would request one.
scenes.image_prompt: Transactional symmetry: two clerks' brass-scaled hands turn a fallen Factor's dark ledger-stone to a lamp, appraising the crystallized column of indecipherable incised glyphs within it. The body lies unattended on white tiles in the lower third of the frame, ignored. A tarnished verdigris bell hangs still behind. Cold procedure over grief, the lit appraised stone the focal heart, the hands and stone kept clear of the top edge, the body low and partial.

scenes.narration: Found short, you were liquidated like any other position. Your death became inventory — editable, mountable, a dim little crystal someone will buy and improve. The gavel came up over you. You are the wrong past surviving while you hold no position in it: the exact nightmare you priced, now priced against you, going once to the floor.
scenes.image_prompt: Mid shot of a body dragged toward the chalk-line of the Exchange while an Auctioneer-Adept lifts a salt-glass gavel over a tide-sledge block. On a bronze stand rests a dim crystal holding the dead Factor's faint, fading image. Verdigris-clad bidders gather across the wet flat in the haze. Cold spectacle of liquidation, the raised gavel and dim crystal the focal pair, the body low in the frame, all subjects kept clear of the top and bottom edges.

scenes.narration: And on the margin, where the reading began, your apprentice stands grown and in the red. The House watches them press a blank dark stone into a fist too small to close, and knot the cord at the small wrist. Now you know who does the pressing, and why. The Exchange has already moved on — only chalk-marks, a haze of iodine, coin-cut salt on the bare crust where the bazaar stood. The book is closed. The chain holds. Next account.
scenes.image_prompt: Wide closing rhyme of the opening: a grown Factor on the receding margin presses a blank black ledger-stone into a foundling's fist too small to close around it, knotting the brine-cord at the small wrist. Behind them only smeared chalk parcel-marks of indecipherable scratches and a thinning haze of iodine drift over bare crust where the bazaar stood. The doubled rust sun low. Quiet indictment, the pressed blank stone the dark focal heart, both figures kept clear of the bottom edge.
